bugs: If a subscriber is deleted while its job is still queued, the job ends up in failed_jobs with a ModelNotFoundException. There is no DeleteWhenMissingModels (confirmed with a probe).

Duplicates are only suppressed for 30 minutes. If the backlog lasts longer, the claim and the UniqueFor lock both expire and a second job gets queued (a probe showed 2 jobs). The fresh() check stops the second CRM call only if the first job has already finished.
The atomic claim update at app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:26-29 leaves out whereNull('crm_synced_at'), so a row synced between the select and the claim can still be queued (minor race).
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:43-48 keeps the try/catch with Log::error and rethrow. The worker already reports the exception, so every attempt is logged twice, and crm_last_error is written on every attempt. A failed() hook would be cleaner.

app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:16 replaces the existing WithoutOverlapping middleware with ShouldBeUnique. Overlap protection only partly survives, and the job now uses two dedup mechanisms (the DB claim plus the unique lock) that have to stay in sync.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:81 says it tests resync after an outage, but it just calls handle() twice. travel() has no effect there and the dispatcher is never involved.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:113 checks instanceof ShouldBeUnique, which tests structure rather than behaviour.
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the swallowed exception, the dispatcher re-queueing rows already in flight, the default 24h withoutOverlapping mutex, and chunk() skipping rows while the filter column is being updated (fixed with chunkById).
Atomic per-row claim with lazyById, plus a fresh() guard against syncing twice.
The broadest test suite: a real failed_jobs test through queue:work, stale-claim tests driven by travel(), a 250-row chunk regression test, and a schedule-lock assertion.
A probe confirmed recovery: after the claim expires, the dispatcher re-queues the subscriber and the sync succeeds.

bugs: Duplicates are only suppressed for 15 minutes (CLAIM_MINUTES). If the backlog runs longer, the subscriber is queued again. The handle() fresh() guard and WithoutOverlapping limit the impact, but duplicate jobs can still pile up during a long outage.
The atomic claim update re-checks whereNull('crm_synced_at'), so no correctness bug was found in the claim logic.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:17 packs five attributes onto the class (Tries(8) + MaxExceptions(3) + Backoff + Timeout + DeleteWhenMissingModels). Each one has a reason (WithoutOverlapping releases count against tries), but it adds tuning surface and quietly changes the original tries=3.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:23,29 repeats the stale-claim where closure. A local scope or a shared closure would remove that.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:44 calls failed() by hand with a made-up exception instead of letting the worker trigger it. The later failed_jobs test covers the real path anyway.
The test file's imports are out of order (Http comes before Console\Scheduling).
strengths: The cleanest fix for problem 1: the try/catch is removed so exceptions reach the worker, and failed() records crm_last_error once the job has given up. Retries and failed_jobs now work as intended.

Keeps the existing WithoutOverlapping middleware but configures it properly (releaseAfter/expireAfter). Pairing it with Tries(8)+MaxExceptions(3) means lock contention cannot burn through the retry budget (verified with a probe: 4 lock-contention releases followed by a successful sync, nothing in failed_jobs).
DeleteWhenMissingModels drops jobs for deleted subscribers instead of sending them to failed_jobs (verified with a probe).

Atomic per-row claim with lazyById, a stale-claim window so failed syncs are re-queued later (a probe confirmed recovery after 16 minutes), chunkById for the normalizer, and withoutOverlapping(10) for the schedule.
Tests cover all four problems, including a real queue:work test that ends in failed_jobs and a 250-row chunk regression test.

v.rationale:
Both implementations find the same four root causes and fix them in much the same way: exceptions are rethrown so retries and failed_jobs work, the dispatcher claims each row atomically and re-queues it once the claim goes stale, the scheduler uses withoutOverlapping(10) instead of the default 24h mutex, and the normalizer uses chunkById. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 11 tests, impl-1: 14 tests). Probes confirmed that both recover after an outage once the claim expires.

impl-2 is ahead on the job itself. It removes the try/catch that swallowed exceptions and moves error recording into a failed() hook. It keeps the existing WithoutOverlapping middleware but configures it properly, and MaxExceptions stops lock-contention releases from burning the retry budget. DeleteWhenMissingModels handles subscribers deleted mid-queue; a probe showed impl-1 sends that case to failed_jobs. impl-1 keeps the catch-log-rethrow pattern, which logs every attempt twice and writes crm_last_error each time. It also swaps WithoutOverlapping for ShouldBeUnique, which layers two dedup mechanisms. Its claim update also skips the crm_synced_at re-check.

impl-1 has more and partly better tests: stale-claim tests driven by travel() and a failed_jobs run through queue:work. But its 'after an outage' test never exercises the dispatcher, and the ShouldBeUnique test only checks the class structure. impl-2 is somewhat heavier on attributes, but each one has a reason. Overall impl-2 ranks first by a small margin.
